title: WPCRL/688/2017 of Gagan Alias Jitendra Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 688 of 2017
Gagan @ Jitendra Ö..Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & Ors. Ö.Respondents
Ms. Neetu Singh, Advocate for the petitioner
Mr. V.S. Pal, A.G.A. assisted by Mr. Prem Kaushal, Brief Holder for the State.
Dated:12.05.2017
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.
Petitioner has approached this Court seeking
the following reliefs:-
ìa) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature
of certiorari commanding the respondents to
quash the impugned first information report
dated 14.04.2017 bearing case crime no.170 of
2017 under section 147, 148, 149, 332, 309,
353, 427, 504, 341 of IPC, 7 Criminal Law
Amendment Act and 3/4 Prevention of Damage
to Public Property Act, 1984 at Police Station
Kotwali Manglore, District Haridwar (contained
as Annexure no.1 to this writ petition) in the
interests of justice.
b) Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction
in the nature of mandamus commanding and
directing the respondent no.2 not to arrest the
petitioner in connection with impugned first
information report dated 14.04.2017 bearing
case crime no.170 of 2017 under section 147,
148, 149, 332, 309, 353, 427, 504, 341 of IPC,
7 Criminal Law Amendment Act and 3/4
Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act,
1984 at Police Station Kotwali Manglore, District
Haridwar (contained as Annexure no.1 to this
writ petition).î
2. On 14.04.2017, an F.I.R. was registered at
Police Station Manglaur, District Haridwar, alleging
therein that various persons (17 named persons and
100-150 unknown persons) were agitating against an
act committed by some miscreants who had set on fire
the poster/banner of Dr. Bhim Rao Ambedkar. It was

2
alleged that these persons caused traffic jam in the
said area and when police tried to persuade them the
said mob became violent and raised slogans. It was
also alleged that some persons from the mob gave
kerosene to one Rajnish who poured the same upon
him and tried to set him on fire. When the police tried
to restrain him, the mob started to throw stones on the
police team in which some police officials received
injuries.
3. It is the submission of learned counsel for
the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent and has
falsely been implicated in the instant crime. She
further submitted that the role assigned to the
petitioner in the F.I.R. is to instigate the mob while the
truth is that petitioner was making efforts to calm
down the charged mob.
4. The Honíble Apex Court, in the case of State
of West Bengal. Vs. Swapna Kumar, 1982 (1) SCC
561, has held that if an offence is disclosed, Court will
not normally interfere with the investigation into the
case, and will permit investigation into the offence
alleged to be completed. If the FIR, prima facie,
discloses the commission of an offence, the Court does
not normally stop the investigation, for, to do so would
be to trench upon the lawful power of the police to
investigate into cognizable offences.
5. I have considered the submissions of learned
counsel for the petitioner and have gone through the
contents of the F.I.R. Contents of the F.I.R. prima facie
disclose the commission of offence. In my opinion, it is

3
not a fit case where the Court should interfere under
Article 226 of the Constitution of India. It is for the
Investigating Officer to investigate the matter and
thereafter to file either the charge sheet or final report
in the matter.
6. The writ petition is devoid of merit and the
same is hereby dismissed. However, it is provided that
if the petitioner surrenders before the court concerned
and seeks bail, his bail application shall be heard and
decided, very very expeditiously, if possible on the
same when it is presented. [Stay application CLMA No.
4898 of 2017 also stands dismissed].
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
 12.05.2017
Rajni
